note: Camden: NEJM 2020 (Finkelstein) found no effect; no published subgroup benefit or '40+ communities' figure found. OneCare formed 2012.
pairs: Post-trial analysis revealed important nuance: the intervention showed significant benefit for patients with behavioral health comorbidities and unstable housing — populations where social needs were driving utilization — but no benefit for patients whose repeated utilization reflected purely clinical complexity. The null overall result masked heterogeneous treatment effects.

The intervention group's 180-day readmission rate was 62.3%, against 61.7% for usual care. The authors suggested that care management for medically and socially complex patients may be limited by access to community resources such as housing and addiction treatment.

The Coalition redesigned its intervention to focus explicitly on patients with modifiable social needs driving utilization, and has documented improved outcomes in this sub-population. More broadly, the hotspotting model has been replicated in 40+ communities nationally.
The Coalition has since revised its model and expanded its national work on complex care.
Subsequent redesign targeting most amenable sub-populations
